summary:
Same-sex sexual relations are lawful in Liechtenstein.

Anti-discrimination law prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation. Gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics are not covered by any anti-discrimination statute in force.

Protection on grounds of sexual orientation includes criminal prohibitions. Since 1 April 2016 harassment and incitement to hatred on grounds of sexual orientation have been banned. Section 283(1) of the Penal Code punishes public incitement to hatred or discrimination on grounds including sexual orientation with imprisonment of up to two years. Section 283(6) prohibits discrimination in public facilities on grounds including sexual orientation.

No procedure exists for changing a legal gender marker in official documents.

No law restricts access to sex-segregated facilities on the basis of gender identity.

Civil marriage and joint adoption have been available to same-sex couples since January 2025.
tangentialFactors:
In a New Year interview reported in January 2016, Prince Hans-Adam II described rainbow families as irresponsible, asserted that children have a right to a normal family, and suggested that Liechtenstein could ignore an adverse ruling of the European Court of Human Rights. The local LGBT organisation Flay said it was shocked by the remarks. The Freie Liste described the remarks as contrary to the Constitution and the European Convention on Human Rights.

The September 2022 parliamentary motion recorded that the Prince had said in 2021 that he had nothing against marriage equality except adoption.

Roman Catholicism is the state religion in Liechtenstein, and the archbishop publicly opposed marriage equality.

The first Pride in Liechtenstein was held in 2022.

In September 2022 members of the Landtag introduced the Motion zur Öffnung der Ehe für alle, which sought to open civil marriage regardless of gender and sexual orientation and to remove remaining legal differences. The motion described registered partnership as perceived as a second-class marriage.
localsOnly:
On 22 February 2005 responsibility for discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation was assigned to the Department of Equal Opportunities (Stabsstelle für Chancengleichheit).

The Act on Media (Mediengesetz), enacted in October 2005, declares media content illegal where it incites or supports discrimination on grounds including sexual orientation.

Medical interventions on the genitals of intersex children are not prohibited by law.
outOfScopeNotes:
Entry and visa requirements relating to gender markers, airport and border screening practice, and access to gender-affirming care for visitors are not sourced in the inventory.

Enforcement data for hate-crime and anti-discrimination provisions in cases involving trans victims, and verifiable data on trans-specific violence, are not sourced in the inventory.
